PROCUREMENT SCAM

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We expose sophisticated procurement scam that is crippling small businesses across SA

Unique Selling Point:
CLASSIC CARTE BLANCHE INVESTIGATION

A NATIONAL SCAM THAT HAS NEVER BEEN EXPOSED OR EXPLAINED - GREAT CONSUMER STORY WITH MANY LAYERS

FOR A CHANGE GOVERNMENT DEPARTMENTS ARE NOT THE CROOKS..... THEY ARE MERELY A PAWN IN A VERY ELABORATE CON!

Summary:
Small Businesses are targeted to provide specialist equipment to government and more recently private industry – the orders are not real – it’s just a con to get the businesses to pay huge deposits.

We follow the change, connect the dots and expose the web of deception behind this con.


Further information:
HOW THE SCAM WORKS:
Basically the scamsters contact companies claiming to be from a government department – they use official looking documentation with letterheads and logos. The scamsters tell the company they are targeting, that they have won a tender to supply a certain product but they have to use a specific supplier – the supplier is NOT legitimate and is part of the scam. The innocent company then places an order with the “supplier” and pays over a large sum of money. OBVIOUSLY no goods ever arrive, nor does payment from government because it wasn’t a real contract – but the money paid to the so-called supplier is already gone.

They are clever web developers – they create websites that are the only suppliers of these specialist products – that way they ensure the deals come to them. A lot of work actually goes into con itself.

WHERE ARE THESE SO-CALLED SUPPLIERS?
The majority is based in PE and CAPE TOWN – all using fake addresses. Landlines that work and cell numbers. They are usually based in a different province to the small business that they are targeting – the purpose of this is that the small business won’t be able to visit the premises.

NEW TREND
Recently the fraudsters have moved on from using government departments details and are now using private companies like Barlo World and Anglo Americans details to con small businesses.

INSIDER
I have a Private Investigator that has been on these cases for over a year – he has traced one of the cellphone numbers and found a woman who poses as the supplier for a West African man. She will do an interview with us to explain how they run the scam. Apparently, the kingpin employs women to take the calls and orders. She is linked to case where the so-called supplier was based in Cape Town.

CASE STUDY ONE
GARETH LAWRENCE – APRIL 2017 – LOST R150 000 and has had to take a new job because the con closed his business.

It was his first ever contract with the Department of Health – everything looked legit. He found a supplier company for the specialist surgical lights – submitted all the documentation to the Department of Health, placed the order with the supplier – transferring a R150 000!

THE REALITY
1. The so-called Department of Health was not legitimate – it was a conartist posing ast the department with fake letterheads and details.
2. The supplier company is part of the con – there are no surgical lights – they just want the deposit. They claim to be based in Cape Town – but the address is fake.
3. No parts are delivered, no payment ever comes from the “Department of Health”

WHAT WE CAN DO
This case is very recent – everything took place now in APRIL!
1. We trace the cell numbers & bank account number – we follow up on these details – hopefully leading us to the crooks.
2. We visit the supplier company address in Cape Town – there is nothing there, it’s fake.

CASE STUDY TWO
DONOVAN SCHIPPERS – 2016 /2017 – didn’t loose any money – but has been contacted relentless by different fraudster – and has kept a recent one running. The majority of suppliers are based in PE.

PRIVATE INVESTIGATOR
ANDRE PUTTER
He has been working on these cases for over a year – he has a clear understanding of the modus operandi and is our link to the insider. His most recent case was a concrete company in PE that got conned. It is through this case that he got in touch with the insider. The fake supplier company in this case was based in Cape Town – also a fake address. We are trying to convince them to do an interview as well.

WHAT ARE THE COPS DOING?
NOT MUCH…. These cases are not being consolidated – they are being run separately by different investigators in different provinces. The PE Hawks are quite involved because they

ADDITIONAL INTERVIEWS / ELEMENTS
1. PE HAWKS – to explain the extent of these cons and the syndicate operations.
2. WEB DEVELOPER to explain the level of work that goes into these cons and the web of deception with domain registration that is created and difficulties with tracing them – these conartists are not amateurs.
3. We follow the leads and try and track down the people behind the details and bank accounts.

We don’t need government departments – we can’t contact all of them – we can say in the story that all have been affected and that they have put warning out.





Extra Budget Items:
1. We will need a third day to film - 2 possible three case studies, 3 experts, an insider and the tracing of the crooks
2. The story is in CAPE TOWN, PORT ELIZABETH AND JOHANNESBURG - all three cities are critical to the story - this shows that the scam in run on a national level.
3. Investigation costs for tracing = R6000

Press Release:


Tender Fraud
Through a clever tender fraud scam, small businesses are targeted to provide specialist equipment to government. The orders aren’t real. It’s
just a ploy to get businesses to pay huge deposits. These sophisticated fraudsters have already crippled several businesses who’ve lost
hundreds of thousands. Carte Blanche follows the leads, connects the dots and exposes the web of deception behind this con.

Script:


STRUCTURE – TENDER SCAM

VO: Tender scams are crippling small businesses across South Africa with over 500 million Rand lost to the economy since 2014.

GARETH: You hear people losing millions and millions to Nigerian scams and you think – I will never fall for that – but this, this, this was as legit as you can get. INT7 M13

LINK: This is a sophisticated con that doesn’t aimlessly phish for victims - this is targeted baiting – reeling in small businesses with a con that is engineered from beginning to end – nothing is left to chance. OPENING

VO: Private investigator Andre Putter’s has dealt with these cases every week for the last 18 months, totalling close to R57 million.

ANDRE: // they deal with you on the Internet, they deal with you on a telephone or a cellphone – they never have to meet you… INT1 M3

VO: The scamsters pose fraudulently as government departments who send out email requests for products linked to their fake supplier companies.

LINK: A Big part of what makes this scam is using real government department with their actual addresses on letterheads that make it look legit. GOVERNEMNT

VO: Machado business owner, Nkosazana Mabogo, fell prey to one of these tender scams when she was convinced in 2015 to pay R295 000 for clamps, she believed, she was supplying to the Department of Public Works.

MABOGO: // they were claiming they were people working for the government and they were enticing me INT1 M7

VO: Thinking she was dealing with the real Department of Public Works - Nkosazana sourced a supplier company online – Mega Solar Systems in Cape Town.

MABOGO: I phoned them, they told me they do have these clamps, (laughs) // and they gave their details where to deposit the money for the business and I did!//– I never thought that they might also not be a genuine thing. INT1 M8

VO: But it wasn’t genuine… the company she dealt with doesn’t exist – the business address is parking lot in Cape Town… Soon after transferring the money – the company went off the radar.

Two years later the same scam is still doing the rounds.

CHRISTO: For fraudsters to survive, they have got to adapt. INT1 M1

VO: Cyber Security expert Christo Boshoff says building a criminal empire in the digital age is cheap and easy operate.

CHRISTO: They // have a technology component attached to it – where either themselves or associates are able to develop websites and search engine optimisation techniques // INT1 M1 //

VO: Gareth Lawrence ran a supply company – he received an unsolicited email from scamsters - asking him to supply the Department of Health with surgical lights in February. After a simple Google search he found the product.

GARETH: // and there was only one supplier in Rondebosh in CPT.

VO: Not only did they have stock, they would deliver the product directly to the Department of Health.

GARETH: I got a delivery note from the supplier INT3 M2(?) // I got a phonecall from the Department of Health saying thank you we received the goods. INT1 M5
DEVI: So in your head, the goods are there? INT3 M2(?)
GARETH: There was no reason to doubt them.

LINK: But in reality there are no products, there is no supplier store and there is no tender – it has all an elaborately ploy….. MED SUPPLIERS

VO: The psychology behind the con is to detach the fraudster from the victim – so that the victim believes they are not being manipulated – that they are in control of the deal.

CHRISTO: The less direct influence the fraudster can have with the victim – the better, because the more believable the story becomes. Because //INT3 M2 I am not going to tell where to go to - I am going to give you a code, you go and search for the code and it will lead you to my site – guaranteed.INT4 M2

VO: The supplier website Gareth used was Med Suppliers dot c o dot z a.

LINK: //To see who’s behind the website we check the registery – while there are some basic details – the phone number is missing a digit –but there is an email address – sheikhmorshid@gmail.com. When we put the into google it comes up with quite a bit…. According to Google he is a very gifted psychic and healer – specialising in all sorts of enlargements…. There’s also a number here – lets see if we can call him – a dead end //.

VO: The digital space has become a free for all in criminal circles.

While legitimate government websites end with .gov.za - fraudsters are using domain names that resemble government sites in their efforts to mislead unsuspecting business owners.

CHRISTO: // I can open up a website with anything that I like – if the name if available I can open it, buy the domain and I can call it government – I can call it whatever I like. INT3 M5 // So, it’s a really, really prime platform for fraudsters to operate on – // it’s not controlled. END INT3 M4

VO: Vika Mpisane is from ZADNA – South Africa’s domain name space regulator.

VIKA: Registration of names is automated // INT3 M24 // – there is no one sitting there checking each name that comes through INT3 M24
DEVI: That’s a problem
VIKA: // it’s not a problem that sits with one organisations , you know it’s spread across. INT3 M18
DEVI: As a regulator this is your job first – before ISPs or anyone else.
VIKA: Yes, it is our job – the name part, ja, true. INT3 M16
DEVI: We can stop this before it even starts
VIKA: True, true to a certain extent – this practice is prevalent world wide // it’s almost practically impossible to monitor those names unless you have an army of people… INt3 M27

VO: Using look a like mobile landlines that don’t operate from a fixed address, the scamsters are able to extend their web of deception – making their fake supplier companies look legitimate in the digital world.

ANDRE: they obviously use cellphones with sim cards that have not been rica-ed or landlines that can be diverted away from a fixed address. INT4 M11

VO: Making it difficult to track the culprits.

The police are currently investigating 200 tender scam cases – while arrests have been made, HAWKS Spokesperson Captain Ndivhuwo Mulamu says there have been no successful prosecutions.

DEVI: When arrests are made – do you get to the kingpins or just the foot soldiers?
CAPTAIN: Most of the time we start with foot soldiers - the runners //INT3 M28

VO: Following the money is often key. Gareth paid his R150 000 into a bank account registered to a Hester Dunbar – we traced her to a home in Johannesburg.

UPSOUND: Ma! Carte Blanche are here….

DEVI: What did you think when you’re daughter told you Carte Blanche were looking for you?
HESTER: I thought I was going to have a heart attack – I thought I was going to die…

VO: 72 year old Hester was approached by a man called Chris at a shopping centre. He claimed he worked for government and had a big supply contract.

HESTER: He said, because he can’t open an account – then we will get these little lights for the hospital – he said I don’t have to worry – he will do everything, I just need to open the account for him. INT1 M5
HESTER: // And he said if I open it then he’s going to give me something.
DEVI: Going to give you what? INT 1 M6
HESTER: He said he was going to pay me every month – I told his you’re lying, just like that – you’re lying. Then he said I promise you. INT 1 M6

VO: Desperate and somewhat gullible – Hester believed him.

HESTER: He took my ID – he told me he just want to make a copy// INT1 M14 // He told me they ask you for proof – don’t open – don’t worry – just give it to them like that. INT1 M15

VO: She opened the account with the contact details the man gave her and handed him the ATM card with the pin.

CAPTAIN: We simply call them money mules - who actually rent out their bank account for these crime lords // INT3 M15
DEVI: if someone uses your bank account – you are still responsible? INt3 M17
CAPTAIN: if you do not report such a crime you become a co-conspirator – // – you are also accountable. INt3 M17

DEVI: Do you know you could be implicated? (not sure what she asks)
HESTER: I can’t believe it – I don’t know what to say…. INT1 M25

VO: Chris managed to calm her suspicions even when she asked to visit the business.

HESTER: I said to him where is your business, I want to see it – do you even have a business? And he said, yes, a big business in Horizon // INT1 M10
HESTER: He said I mustn’t go to the business – he doesn’t want them to see me by the business

VO: Hester was given R3000 for the use of her name on the bank account and her silence.

In search of the illusive government official, Chris - we decided to look so-called business in Horison, Roodepoort.

LINK This is the address… let’s see if we can find Chris
DEVI: I’m looking for Chris?

VO: Apparently no man lives there, just a woman.

DEVI: So there’s no business here? No selling medical equipment?

LINK: The Kingpins cleverly distance themselves from every element in the con – they are not ones who the emails, neither are the ones that pose as the government officials or the fake suppliers company. KINGPINS

ANDRE: He’s pulling the strings and he’s collecting the money and if somebody gets caught along the way it will be one of these employees he can just dispose of. // INT7 M3

DEVI: How do you feel?
HESTER: Bloody stupid! INt1 M27
HESTER: I thought jissie that’s a big favour and he is going to pay me – I’m honest I did need money (weepy) INT2 M7

VO: While desperation and greed fuel these types of cons – Nkosazana says she has learnt her lesson but she worries that these fraudsters are not behind bars.

MABOGO: they are cunning and very, very heartless and they don’t care – they don’t care how they destroy other people. Even, they don’t care, they don’t care even how much they are destroying our country // it’s like wild fire – burning South Africa into ashes. INT1 M18


PROMOS

PROMO 1
CHRISTO: For fraudsters to survive, they have got to adapt.

VO: Tender scamsters pose as government departments creating a digital web of deception to bring in the cash.

PROMO 2
VO: We expose a sophisticated tender scam that’s crippling small businesses across South Africa.

MABOGO: they are cunning and very, very heartless and they don’t care – they don’t care how they destroy other people

VO: Carte Blanche investigates.

PROMO 3
VO: Sophisticated Tender Cons are reeling in millions of rands from unsuspecting business owners - we track down a money mule used in the scam.

HESTER: I thought jissie that’s a big favour and he is going to pay me – I’m honest I did need money (weepy)

Because //INT3 M2 I am not going to tell where to go to - I am going to give you a code, you go and search for the code and it will lead you to my site – guaranteed.INT4 M2 VO: The supplier website Gareth used was Med Suppliers dot c o dot z a. LINK: //To see who’s behind the website we check the registery – while there are some basic details – the phone number is missing a digit –but there is an email address – sheikhmorshid@gmail.com. When we put the into google it comes up with quite a bit…. According to Google he is a very gifted psychic and healer – specialising in all sorts of enlargements…. There’s also a number here – lets see if we can call him – a dead end //. VO: The digital space has become a free for all in criminal circles. While legitimate government websites end with .gov.za - fraudsters are using domain names that resemble government sites in their efforts to mislead unsuspecting business owners. CHRISTO: // I can open up a website with anything that I like – if the name if available I can open it, buy the domain and I can call it government – I can call it whatever I like. INT3 M5 // So, it’s a really, really prime platform for fraudsters to operate on – // it’s not controlled. END INT3 M4 VO: Vika Mpisane is from ZADNA – South Africa’s domain name space regulator. VIKA: Registration of names is automated // INT3 M24 // – there is no one sitting there checking each name that comes through INT3 M24 DEVI: That’s a problem VIKA: // it’s not a problem that sits with one organisations , you know it’s spread across. INT3 M18 DEVI: As a regulator this is your job first – before ISPs or anyone else. VIKA: Yes, it is our job – the name part, ja, true. INT3 M16 DEVI: We can stop this before it even starts VIKA: True, true to a certain extent – this practice is prevalent world wide // it’s almost practically impossible to monitor those names unless you have an army of people… INt3 M27 VO: Using look a like mobile landlines that don’t operate from a fixed address, the scamsters are able to extend their web of deception – making their fake supplier companies look legitimate in the digital world. ANDRE: they obviously use cellphones with sim cards that have not been rica-ed or landlines that can be diverted away from a fixed address. INT4 M11 VO: Making it difficult to track the culprits. The police are currently investigating 200 tender scam cases – while arrests have been made, HAWKS Spokesperson Captain Ndivhuwo Mulamu says there have been no successful prosecutions. DEVI: When arrests are made – do you get to the kingpins or just the foot soldiers? CAPTAIN: Most of the time we start with foot soldiers - the runners //INT3 M28 VO: Following the money is often key. Gareth paid his R150 000 into a bank account registered to a Hester Dunbar – we traced her to a home in Johannesburg. UPSOUND: Ma! Carte Blanche are here…. DEVI: What did you think when you’re daughter told you Carte Blanche were looking for you? HESTER: I thought I was going to have a heart attack – I thought I was going to die… VO: 72 year old Hester was approached by a man called Chris at a shopping centre. He claimed he worked for government and had a big supply contract. HESTER: He said, because he can’t open an account – then we will get these little lights for the hospital – he said I don’t have to worry – he will do everything, I just need to open the account for him. INT1 M5 HESTER: // And he said if I open it then he’s going to give me something. DEVI: Going to give you what? INT 1 M6 HESTER: He said he was going to pay me every month – I told his you’re lying, just like that – you’re lying. Then he said I promise you. INT 1 M6 VO: Desperate and somewhat gullible – Hester believed him. HESTER: He took my ID – he told me he just want to make a copy// INT1 M14 // He told me they ask you for proof – don’t open – don’t worry – just give it to them like that. INT1 M15 VO: She opened the account with the contact details the man gave her and handed him the ATM card with the pin. CAPTAIN: We simply call them money mules - who actually rent out their bank account for these crime lords // INT3 M15 DEVI: if someone uses your bank account – you are still responsible? INt3 M17 CAPTAIN: if you do not report such a crime you become a co-conspirator – // – you are also accountable. INt3 M17 DEVI: Do you know you could be implicated? (not sure what she asks) HESTER: I can’t believe it – I don’t know what to say…. INT1 M25 VO: Chris managed to calm her suspicions even when she asked to visit the business. HESTER: I said to him where is your business, I want to see it – do you even have a business? And he said, yes, a big business in Horizon // INT1 M10 HESTER: He said I mustn’t go to the business – he doesn’t want them to see me by the business VO: Hester was given R3000 for the use of her name on the bank account and her silence. In search of the illusive government official, Chris - we decided to look so-called business in Horison, Roodepoort. LINK This is the address… let’s see if we can find Chris DEVI: I’m looking for Chris? VO: Apparently no man lives there, just a woman. DEVI: So there’s no business here? No selling medical equipment? LINK: The Kingpins cleverly distance themselves from every element in the con – they are not ones who the emails, neither are the ones that pose as the government officials or the fake suppliers company. KINGPINS ANDRE: He’s pulling the strings and he’s collecting the money and if somebody gets caught along the way it will be one of these employees he can just dispose of. // INT7 M3 DEVI: How do you feel? HESTER: Bloody stupid! INt1 M27 HESTER: I thought jissie that’s a big favour and he is going to pay me – I’m honest I did need money (weepy) INT2 M7 VO: While desperation and greed fuel these types of cons – Nkosazana says she has learnt her lesson but she worries that these fraudsters are not behind bars. MABOGO: they are cunning and very, very heartless and they don’t care – they don’t care how they destroy other people. Even, they don’t care, they don’t care even how much they are destroying our country // it’s like wild fire – burning South Africa into ashes. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We expose sophisticated procurement scam that is crippling small businesses across SA
metadata.Unique Selling Point: CLASSIC CARTE BLANCHE INVESTIGATION A NATIONAL SCAM THAT HAS NEVER BEEN EXPOSED OR EXPLAINED - GREAT CONSUMER STORY WITH MANY LAYERS FOR A CHANGE GOVERNMENT DEPARTMENTS ARE NOT THE CROOKS..... THEY ARE MERELY A PAWN IN A VERY ELABORATE CON!
metadata.Summary: Small Businesses are targeted to provide specialist equipment to government and more recently private industry – the orders are not real – it’s just a con to get the businesses to pay huge deposits. We follow the change, connect the dots and expose the web of deception behind this con.
metadata.Further information: HOW THE SCAM WORKS: Basically the scamsters contact companies claiming to be from a government department – they use official looking documentation with letterheads and logos. The scamsters tell the company they are targeting, that they have won a tender to supply a certain product but they have to use a specific supplier – the supplier is NOT legitimate and is part of the scam. The innocent company then places an order with the “supplier” and pays over a large sum of money. OBVIOUSLY no goods ever arrive, nor does payment from government because it wasn’t a real contract – but the money paid to the so-called supplier is already gone. They are clever web developers – they create websites that are the only suppliers of these specialist products – that way they ensure the deals come to them. A lot of work actually goes into con itself. WHERE ARE THESE SO-CALLED SUPPLIERS? The majority is based in PE and CAPE TOWN – all using fake addresses. Landlines that work and cell numbers. They are usually based in a different province to the small business that they are targeting – the purpose of this is that the small business won’t be able to visit the premises. NEW TREND Recently the fraudsters have moved on from using government departments details and are now using private companies like Barlo World and Anglo Americans details to con small businesses. INSIDER I have a Private Investigator that has been on these cases for over a year – he has traced one of the cellphone numbers and found a woman who poses as the supplier for a West African man. She will do an interview with us to explain how they run the scam. Apparently, the kingpin employs women to take the calls and orders. She is linked to case where the so-called supplier was based in Cape Town. CASE STUDY ONE GARETH LAWRENCE – APRIL 2017 – LOST R150 000 and has had to take a new job because the con closed his business. It was his first ever contract with the Department of Health – everything looked legit. He found a supplier company for the specialist surgical lights – submitted all the documentation to the Department of Health, placed the order with the supplier – transferring a R150 000! THE REALITY 1. The so-called Department of Health was not legitimate – it was a conartist posing ast the department with fake letterheads and details. 2. The supplier company is part of the con – there are no surgical lights – they just want the deposit. They claim to be based in Cape Town – but the address is fake. 3. No parts are delivered, no payment ever comes from the “Department of Health” WHAT WE CAN DO This case is very recent – everything took place now in APRIL! 1. We trace the cell numbers & bank account number – we follow up on these details – hopefully leading us to the crooks. 2. We visit the supplier company address in Cape Town – there is nothing there, it’s fake. CASE STUDY TWO DONOVAN SCHIPPERS – 2016 /2017 – didn’t loose any money – but has been contacted relentless by different fraudster – and has kept a recent one running. The majority of suppliers are based in PE. PRIVATE INVESTIGATOR ANDRE PUTTER He has been working on these cases for over a year – he has a clear understanding of the modus operandi and is our link to the insider. His most recent case was a concrete company in PE that got conned. It is through this case that he got in touch with the insider. The fake supplier company in this case was based in Cape Town – also a fake address. We are trying to convince them to do an interview as well. WHAT ARE THE COPS DOING? NOT MUCH…. These cases are not being consolidated – they are being run separately by different investigators in different provinces. The PE Hawks are quite involved because they ADDITIONAL INTERVIEWS / ELEMENTS 1. PE HAWKS – to explain the extent of these cons and the syndicate operations. 2. WEB DEVELOPER to explain the level of work that goes into these cons and the web of deception with domain registration that is created and difficulties with tracing them – these conartists are not amateurs. 3. We follow the leads and try and track down the people behind the details and bank accounts. We don’t need government departments – we can’t contact all of them – we can say in the story that all have been affected and that they have put warning out.

The story is in CAPE TOWN, PORT ELIZABETH AND JOHANNESBURG - all three cities are critical to the story - this shows that the scam in run on a national level. 3.
